Hi Alex / Priya 

Thanks for the clear asks. Per Marissa's note, I've attached three short artifacts: redwood-sdk-integration-guide.pdf, embeddings-rerank-recommendation.md, and prompt-governance-checklist.md. Below are the highlights we'll walk through on Tue 10/13 (11am PT):

1) SDK setup & auth
- SDKs: we support Python, Node, and Java SDKs. Quickstart in the attached PDF includes sample code for streaming responses and structured output (tool-calling) via the SDK.
- Auth for Private: two-layer approach 
- mTLS between your service and the private control-plane + signed session tokens for per-user calls. mTLS certs can be rotated via your KMS. We support Azure Key Vault and common HSM-backed workflows.
- Example snippet (curl & Python):
  - curl --cert client.crt --key client.key -H 'Authorization: Bearer <session-token>' https://private-acme.redwood.internal/v1/generate
  - Python SDK: see example in PDF for streaming + structured json schema enforcement.

2) Routing & structured output
- Routing: policy-based routing (latency vs cost) is configurable; you can route specific routes to a reranker or to a smaller/cheaper model when confidence passes a threshold.
- Structured output/tool-calling: we recommend validating model output against a JSON schema at the runtime boundary. The SDK supports schema-hints and atomic tool-call hooks to prevent arbitrary execution.

3) Embeddings & rerankers
- Preprocessing: normalize whitespace, remove agent signatures, remove PII placeholders, and chunk by semantic boundaries (~512 tokens per chunk, overlap 50 tokens).
- Embedding model: start with mid-sized models (produces 768-d vectors) and measure recall/latency trade-offs. Use quantized endpoints for batch indexing to reduce cost.
- Reranking pattern: coarse retrieve with embeddings + fine rerank with a smaller cross-attention model for top-N. We'll include benchmark numbers in the deck.

4) Prompt templates & governance
- Versioning: semantic prompt versions (vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) + immutable storage backed by audit logs. Each prompt change requires a prompt change PR with owner, test prompts, and regen metrics.
- Injection mitigations: implement input sanitization layer (remove control sequences), contextual allowlists for tool-calls, and response post-filters that block or flag unexpected instructions.
- Red-teaming: run a monthly red-team for prompt changes and quarterly full-simulation including adversarial user inputs, chain-of-thought leakage tests, and policy-injection scenarios. Capture examples and metrics in our governance dashboard.

Attachments (referenced above):
- redwood-sdk-integration-guide.pdf (integration checklist + snippets)
- embeddings-rerank-recommendation.md (preprocessing + recommended model sizes)
- prompt-governance-checklist.md (versioning + red-team templates)

If helpful, I can include minimal config snippets for mTLS + KMS rotation in the meeting deck. See you Tue.

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
